r1.said: Part 0 ended with hello dot C P P: a box that turns. Here it grows into a real app, one step at a time.

r2.said: Each step is a program that builds and runs, and the window shows what that program draws.

o1.said: Step one: let the user move the camera. Orbit Controls listens to the mouse. Drag to turn, scroll to zoom.

o2.said: And when the window changes size, the camera's aspect and the renderer's size follow, so nothing stretches.

m1.said: Step two: a real model instead of the box. The G L T F loader turns the file into the same kind of tree: meshes, materials and bones.

m2.said: Lit by one light from one side, the rest of him stays black. Real light comes from all around.

k1.said: Step three: light from a photo. One H D R image of a park becomes the background, and what every material reflects.

k2.said: Tone mapping then fits the bright sky into what a screen can show.

a1.said: Step four: motion. The file also holds animations, and a mixer plays the walk on the model's skeleton.

a2.said: Each frame, it moves on by the time since the last frame, so he walks at the same pace on any computer.

h1.said: Step five: shadows. They are off until you ask: turn them on in the renderer, then choose which light and objects cast them, and what receives them.

h2.said: The light sees the scene through a camera of its own. Only what is inside it gets a shadow, so size it to your scene.

n1.said: Step six: two thousand stones. As one mesh each, that is about 960 draw calls every frame, one for every stone in view.

n2.said: An instanced mesh draws them together: one geometry, one material, and a matrix and a colour per stone. Now the frame takes 5 draw calls.

p1.said: Step seven: point at things. The raycaster sends a ray from the camera, through the mouse, into the scene.

p2.said: It returns what the ray hits, nearest first. On an instanced mesh it also says which instance, so one stone can light up.

u1.said: Step eight: knobs. Dear Im Gooey builds a panel in a few lines, and its sliders write straight into your variables.

u2.said: I O Capture keeps the camera still while the mouse is busy with the panel.

c1.said: That is the whole app, 110 lines of C plus plus. It is in the repository as examples, lesson, app dot C P P.

c2.said: Build it with step set to any number from zero to eight, and you get the program as it stood after that step.
